segments.text: JENNIFER CHAYES: And welcome.
Thanks so much for joining us for day two of the agentic AI
summit.
I'm Jennifer Chayes, founding Dean of the UC Berkeley
College of Computing, Data Science, and Society,
or CDSS, as we call it.
It contains EECS and statistics and a few other computational
domain departments.
I'm a professor of EECS, statistics, math,
and information.
We conceived of CDSS as the platform both
to advance the core of EECS and statistics,
and to connect them with other disciplines
across campus, from letters and Sciences
to law, medicine and health policy and more.
We were born at the perfect time, half a year
after the release of chat--
half a year after the release of ChatGPT.
We are the first new college at Berkeley since the 1960s.
So the AI transformation is the perfect time
to have a new college.
We see our college as the place to seize opportunities
and mitigate potential harms of these powerful technologies
cognizant of the fact that we are only
in the very, very early days.
At the summit today we'll discuss the latest research,
diverse applications across industries, the opportunities,
and the safety and security challenges
inherent in AI systems.
You likely know that much of the foundational AI underlying
these recent leaps and bounds was done by Berkeley EECS
faculty and students.
Indeed, the faculty and students of our college
and that many of them are in leadership positions driving it
forward.
I would assume that we have a lot of alumni
out in the audience here today.
We've shown that bringing smart people, diverse talent,
and expert perspectives together provides community immunity
and leads to more informed and responsible innovation.
This summit provides an opportunity
to build bridges across communities,
catalyze meaningful conversations and partnerships,
and collaborate in the transformation of the future.
While AI developments are increasingly
being done behind closed doors, I'm
here to say that we need to maintain open doors
and conversations among those developing and advancing
this technology.
We need open source models in order
to bring the benefits of AI to all, not just the select few.
As some of you probably know, Berkeley has been the home
and leader in open source technology since the 1970s,
and we're doubling down on open for the AI models.
Not only open source, but also open weight and even open data
when possible.
We want to partner with the government,
other academic institutions, nonprofits, and companies
that are aligned.
The only way that this country can maintain--
and in fact, much of the world can maintain its lead in AI
and the innovation economy is to grow our open weight AI models.
At our college, Berkeley CDSS, in addition
to building foundational AI systems that are open,
we're focused on AI security and safety, which many of you
heard about yesterday, alternative AI models
and architectures that will lower the energy
consumption that we are constantly-- that we are seeing
in our data centers, and we are focused on AI models
where data is particularly sparse, including
AI for science.
And in fact, for most domains beyond language, images,
and video.
The next decade, we're going to see more advances
with positive impacts for humanity
in biomedicine and health, climate and sustainability,
and other areas.
Our college has created leading institutes in AI
for medicine and health, for biomedicine, for materials,
and more.
At the same time, education is completely
shifting in the age of AI, and Berkeley
is at the forefront of this change.
We're using AI to level the playing field for students
coming into the University, and we
are teaching our students how to work in human AI hybrid teams.
As others mentioned yesterday, we
believe that AI will lead to New kinds of jobs that will involve
these hybrid teams working at the boundary of what
is currently possible.
We need the community gathered here
to engage by advancing technology
that amplifies our collective potential
and actively empowers individuals in society.
We're hosted by the UC Berkeley Center
for Responsible Decentralized Intelligence, RDI,
led by the amazing Dawn Song.
Dawn, thanks for gathering this group together today
and for your important contributions in AI safety
and agentic AI education.
Let's welcome Dawn.
[APPLAUSE]
